tags.description: The eight limbs of yoga according to Patanjali

tags.name: Yamas
tags.description: Ethical restraints - how we relate to others

tags.name: Niyamas
tags.description: Personal observances - how we relate to ourselves

flashcards.title: Yamas
flashcards.short_answer: Ethical restraints or "how we relate to others".
flashcards.definition: These are the social disciplines that guide our interactions with the world around us. They include five specific practices (Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Brahmacarya, and Aparigraha) that help us act with awareness rather than reacting out of habit or vice.

flashcards.title: Niyamas
flashcards.short_answer: Personal observances or "how we relate to ourselves".
flashcards.definition: These are internal practices and disciplines meant to improve our own character and being. They consist of Sauca, Samtosa, Tapas, Svadhaya, and Isharapranidhana, focusing on internal cleanliness, contentment, and devotion.

flashcards.title: Asana
flashcards.short_answer: Physical postures; literally meaning "to sit" or "being seated".
flashcards.definition: Originally referring to sitting with a master to receive knowledge, it has evolved into the physical practice of postures. The goal is to find a balance between Sthira (steadiness/effort) and Sukha (comfort/ease) so the body is alert but unstressed.

flashcards.title: Pranayama
flashcards.short_answer: Breath control and the regulation of life force.
flashcards.definition: This practice involves joining the breath with movement to integrate the body and mind. It includes techniques like Ujjayi (calming) or Kapalabhati (energizing) to help the mind become slower, deeper, and more focused.

flashcards.title: Pratyahara
flashcards.short_answer: Withdrawal of the senses; not chasing the "shiny object".
flashcards.definition: It is the practice of filtering out external distractions to focus inward. For example, when a siren goes off during savasana, you use Pratyahara to stay present in your practice rather than following the noise.

flashcards.title: Dharana
flashcards.short_answer: Concentration; holding the mind in one direction.
flashcards.definition: We create the conditions to focus the mind's attention on a single object, like the breath, a candle, or a mandala. This prevents the "monkey mind" from jumping in many different directions.

flashcards.title: Dhyana
flashcards.short_answer: Meditation; a continuous flow of concentration.
flashcards.definition: In this state, the mind moves in one direction like a quiet river. You perceive an object and focus only on it, forming a deep communication where nothing else is happening.

flashcards.title: Samadhi
flashcards.short_answer: Union; becoming one with the object of meditation.
flashcards.definition: This is the experience of realizing non-dualistic existence, seeing things clearly without the Maya (illusion). It is pure flow where you are no longer a separate physical creature but are united with the divine or the fabric of the universe.

flashcards.title: Ahimsa
flashcards.definition: This is the practice of justice and non-violence toward all beings. In yoga class, it means finding a balance with Satya—for example, not pushing yourself or a student so hard that it causes injury, but also not avoiding the truth of where growth is needed.

flashcards.title: Satya
flashcards.definition: This involves being honest with ourselves and others. As a teacher, it means providing "radical candor" or a "+1 nudge" to help students see their flaws and grow, provided the feedback comes from a sincere, caring place.

flashcards.title: Asteya
flashcards.definition: Beyond just not taking physical objects, it involves not stealing others' time or energy. It is a reminder to avoid vices and distractions, focusing instead on what we have earned.

flashcards.title: Brahmacarya
flashcards.short_answer: Responsible behavior; moderation of the senses.
flashcards.definition: Often interpreted as respect for family life and not overdoing sexual pleasure, it is a subtle call to move toward the truth through responsible, disciplined behavior.

flashcards.title: Aparigraha
flashcards.short_answer: Non-greed or non-attachment; only taking what is necessary.
flashcards.definition: This means not taking advantage of a situation and only taking what you have earned. It is the practice of non-coveting, which helps us stay away from addiction and ego-centrism.

flashcards.title: Sauca
flashcards.short_answer: Cleanliness; purity of body and mind.
flashcards.definition: This includes internal cleanliness (proper eating and breathing) and external cleanliness in our physical environment. It is about getting rid of "rubbish" in the body through healthy habits.

flashcards.title: Samtosa
flashcards.short_answer: Contentment; being okay with what is.
flashcards.definition: To be content with what we already have and to accept outcomes even when they don't meet our expectations. It is the appreciation of what did happen rather than focusing on what we wanted to happen.

flashcards.title: Tapas
flashcards.short_answer: Discipline or "heat"; keeping the body fit.
flashcards.definition: The activity of "heating" the body through posture and breath to cleanse it. It is the effort and discipline required to maintain health and burn away impurities.

flashcards.title: Svadhaya
flashcards.definition: This is the study of ancient texts and the examination of one's own inner dialogue. It is an inquiry into who is "living in you" and identifying the labels we carry that are not our true identity.

flashcards.title: Isharapranidhana
flashcards.definition: Literally meaning to "lay all your actions at the feet of God," it involves offering the "fruits of your labor" to something larger than yourself. It is the realization that you are not the most important thing and surrendering to the divine.
